draft.title: Medicare
card: Medicare is Australia's public health insurance scheme. It is run by the Australian Government and is open to eligible residents.
It is funded mainly from general taxes, including the Medicare levy, which is a small part of a person's taxable income.
Medicare covers or subsidises the cost of many services, such as visits to doctors, tests like blood tests and X-rays, and care as a public patient in a public hospital.
A subsidy means Medicare pays some or all of the fee. A patient may still pay a gap if the provider charges more than the Medicare amount.
draft.remember: Medicare is tax-funded public insurance that helps pay for doctors, tests and public hospital care.

a.q: Which statement best describes how Medicare is paid for?
opts: Mostly from taxes, including the Medicare levy
Mostly from fees paid each time someone sees a doctor
Mostly from premiums paid to private companies
Mostly from donations given to public hospitals
a.why: Medicare is funded mainly from taxes, and the Medicare levy is part of that. Premiums go to private health insurers, which is a different scheme, so that option is wrong.
a.clue: Think about what people pay through their income.

b.q: Tom has a blood test ordered by his GP in Bendigo. The provider charges more than the Medicare amount. What is true about this case?
opts: Medicare pays its part and Tom may pay the gap
Medicare pays nothing because the fee is too high
Medicare pays the full fee, however high it is
Medicare pays only if Tom has private insurance
b.why: Medicare subsidises tests, so it pays its set amount. If the provider charges more, Tom may pay the gap. Medicare does not pay any fee in full, and it does not depend on private insurance.
b.clue: A subsidy pays some of the fee, not always all of it.

a.best: Mostly from taxes, including the Medicare levy

b.best: Medicare pays its part and Tom may pay the gap

problems.detail: Why (b) says 'Medicare does not pay any fee in full'. This is false and contradicts the card, which says Medicare pays 'some or all of the fee'. Bulk-billed services and public hospital care as a public patient are fully covered.

The right option is the only one with a hedged qualifier ('may'). The distractors all use absolutes ('full fee, however high', 'nothing', 'only'), so a student could pick the right answer by elimination without knowing the idea.
The right option is the only one that repeats 'Medicare' from the stem ('the Medicare levy'). Together with the clue about income, this points to the answer without testing understanding.
